title: system_server Boot and System Service Architecture Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies system_server boot and system service architecture?
options: Separate local framework facades from remote service authority and account for Binder, permissions, boot readiness, latency, and failure.
Assume all services share one thread
questions.answer: Separate local framework facades from remote service authority and account for Binder, permissions, boot readiness, latency, and failure.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: Every Android system service runs as a Java object inside system_server.
questions.explanation: Calling getSystemService returns a local manager object, but assuming all work is local hides Binder latency, remote failure, permission checks, and system ownership.

questions.prompt: What does a framework manager object usually represent?
questions.answer: A local client facade or proxy for state and operations owned by a framework service, often across Binder.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
